title: GHA Indie Worker HTTP error and pagination envelope
$comment: HUMAN-AUTHORED PEER AUTHORITY of the error and pagination models in contracts/typespec/http.tsp. Neither is generated from the other. The HTTP *bindings* (routes, verbs, status codes) live only in TypeSpec: JSON Schema cannot express them, and inventing a vendor keyword to fake the comparison would make the parity claim weaker, not stronger. See contracts/README.md.

ErrorCode.description: Same vocabulary the session protocol closes with, so a client has one error table for both transports.

ErrorDetail.description: One machine-readable detail of a failure, naming the offending field.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the offending member of the request, e.g. `/labels/3`.

ApiError.description: The single error shape every operation returns. `code` is the same vocabulary the session protocol closes with, so a client has one error table for both transports.

message.description: Human-readable, safe to log. Never contains credentials or request bodies.

requestId.description: Correlates with the `request-id` response header and the trace. `runtime` puts it in every log line.

onboarding.description: Present on a 409 from an onboarding operation. Lets a client tell `no_seats_available` from `last_owner` without parsing `message`.

PageInfo.description: Cursor pagination envelope. Cursors are opaque; a client that parses one is relying on an implementation detail.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

hasMore.description: True when a further page exists. Equivalent to `nextCursor` being present, stated so a client need not infer it.

role.description: Never above the caller's own role; `runtime::tenancy` refuses escalation.

Realm.description: Which identity realm a token came from. A token is only ever valid in one. `runtime::authz::Realm`.

Audience.description: The audience a service introspects FOR. Introspecting without an audience is how a token minted for one service gets replayed against another, so every call names one. `runtime::authz::Audience`.

Principal.description: The caller a handler actually sees, after introspection. `runtime::authz::VerifiedActor`. The realm/audience pair is checked before this value exists, so a handler holding one cannot be serving the wrong plane.

subject.description: Subject claim, stable for the life of the account.

orgId.description: Org the token is scoped to. Absent for an individual account with no org.

role.description: Role in `orgId`. Present exactly when `orgId` is.

OnboardingErrorCode.description: Why an onboarding step was refused. One variant per `runtime::tenancy::OnboardingError`, so a client can branch on the same set the domain does instead of matching on prose.

OnboardingFailure.description: The structured half of an onboarding refusal. `OnboardingError` carries payload on three of its variants; those are the optional fields here, and a client reads only the ones its `reason` defines.

actorRole.description: Set when `reason` is `role_escalation`: the role the caller holds.

grantedRole.description: Set when `reason` is `role_escalation`: the role they tried to grant.
